data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004's distinguishing evidence—'justified deviations' where the non-expert panel marks an item N/A or incorrect with a valid rationale—presupposes precisely the domain expertise the problem withholds. The task is about TRAINED NON-EXPERTS; by definition they lack the conceptual framework to reliably recognize when a checklist item is genuinely inapplicable versus merely appearing so. So the proposed signal is not causally available to the agent population under evaluation. Worse, within a single evaluation, a non-expert deviation could itself be mere checklist-compliance-adjacent noise that happens to align with the right answer—the very confound the target is supposed to distinguish—yet the target's evidence criterion would classify it as a genuine reliability gain simply because a rationale was attached. The target thus fails to identify evidence that actually separates genuine gain from compliance-tracking for the specified population.
